history.summary: The Dangaria Baba Temple is a Shiva shrine built around the base of a banyan tree said to be over 150 years old, at Raneghat near the Siang Bridge on the Pasighat-Pangin road (NH-13). Puja began in 1962 when PWD engineers constructing the road held protective pujas after a series of unexplained accidents; the accidents reportedly ceased, cementing the site's reputation as a place of divine protection (abotanitv.in, itanagartimes.com). The annual Dangaria Baba Mela on the last Saturday of every year draws thousands of devotees from across Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, including Dibrugarh, Silapathar and Jonai, as well as followers of Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Buddhism and Donyi-Polo. A renovation and extension with a larger structure housing all gods and goddesses was announced (foundation laid December 31, 2020).

town_description: Pasighat is the oldest town of Arunachal Pradesh (established 1911) and the headquarters of East Siang district, on the banks of the Siang River. It is the gateway to the state and is known for the Kekar Monying hanging bridge, the Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary, and the culture of the Adi people.

travel.road: On NH-13 (Pasighat-Pangin Main Road) at Raneghat, near the Siang Bridge

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; best on the last Saturday of December for the annual mela
